summary: This regulation explains who must follow Chapter V of the rules. It applies only to companies that have listed specific non-convertible securities on a recognised stock exchange. It also clarifies how words like interest, dividend, and default are understood in these rules.
points: The entity must have listed its non-convertible securities on a recognised stock exchange.
The listing must follow the Securities and Exchange Board of India Regulations, 2021.
The entity must read references to interest as dividend if it lists certain preference shares or similar instruments.
The entity must treat any non-payment of interest, dividend, or principal on the pre-agreed date as a default.
The entity must recognise a default at the very first instance of a delay in servicing payments.
example: Sunrise Steel Limited listed its non-convertible securities on a recognised stock exchange following the official 2021 regulations. Because of this listing, the company falls directly under the rules of Chapter V. Later, Sunrise Steel faced a temporary cash flow crunch and delayed a scheduled interest payment to its investors by just one day past the pre-agreed date. Under these rules, that single day of delay is immediately recognised as a default. If Sunrise Steel had instead listed non-convertible redeemable preference shares, any rule mentioning interest would simply apply to its dividend instead.

terms.meaning: Financial instruments issued by a company that cannot be converted into equity shares.
An official marketplace approved by the government or SEBI for buying and selling securities.
Failing to pay the full interest, dividend, or principal amount on the pre-agreed date.

watch: A common confusion is thinking a default only happens after a long grace period, whereas these rules state it is recognised at the very first instance of delay.
